overview: The Housing Unhoused Disabled Veterans Act changes how income is counted for a federal program that helps homeless veterans pay rent. That program, known as HUD-VASH, pairs rental vouchers from the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) with case management from the Department of Veterans Affairs. Under the bill, veterans' disability compensation from the VA would no longer count as income when deciding whether a veteran qualifies for the program, though it would still be used when calculating how much rent they pay. The same exclusion would apply when HUD-VASH households seek other housing help, and for new HUD-assisted housing built on VA property after the bill becomes law. As of February 11, 2025, the House had passed it and it was before the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee.
for: Supporters say counting disability payments as income can push some homeless veterans just over the eligibility limit, and that the bill keeps veterans from losing housing help because of benefits they earned through their service.
against: Critics say widening eligibility for a program with a limited number of vouchers could mean longer waits for the lowest-income veterans and families who already qualify.
